notes: Hard bucket (18/30). A multi-stage pipeline in one container where every later stage depends on an earlier one: (1) build and install from its source tree the platform's own, from-scratch, clean-room Zephyr compiler (a small single-pass C-like compiler whose only source is the tree in the image) and expose it as /app/cc/bin/cc; (2) use that freshly built compiler to compile the bundled Zephyr drift decoder; (3) reverse-engineer the drift frame grammar from the decoder and author a byte-exact general encoder (RLE frames plus 1..128-byte literal frames, run-splitting at the 128-byte boundary, last-buffer boundary guards) that reproduces arbitrary payloads byte-for-byte; (4) gate the public header behind a strict -std=c++11 probe. The encoder must generalize: the verifier pushes hidden payloads (long RLE runs, an exact literal boundary, binary with NUL and 0xFF, high-entropy regions) through /app/pack then /app/unpack and requires byte-identical output, so an encoder hard-coded to the visible corpus fails. Difficulty is genuine (dependent_stages + hidden_case_generalization + debugging_ambiguity on malformed frames), not prompt length.
